narrativeReportMd:
# RelatedArtifact R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
R6 keeps the same `RelatedArtifact` datatype identity, but it has a local hard R4-to-R6 instance break because `RelatedArtifact.url` is removed. The largest migration theme is a representation redesign: R6 introduces `resourceReference` and `artifact[x]`, deprecates the older `citation`, `document`, and `resource` carriers, and adds reference-based forms that do not round-trip cleanly to R4.

## Scope
The analysis used the supplied R4/R6 StructureDefinitions, package indexes, package metadata, and the local `related-artifact-type` ValueSet/CodeSystem files. Inherited `Element`/`DataType` hierarchy changes are out of scope for this datatype report.

## Main migration themes
Existing R4 instances that populate `url` need transformation because R6 has no same-name field and `artifact[x]` has no primitive `url` choice. R6 instances may use `artifactReference`, `resourceReference`, or the new `part-of` type code, all of which can fail R4 validation or require lossy extension-based down-conversion. R6 also adds warning-level constraints that turn some previously unconstrained combinations of `type` and artifact carrier into validator warnings.

## Highest-impact findings
The hard break is `RelatedArtifact.url` removal. The high R6-to-R4 risks are the new representation choices and the required terminology addition `part-of`.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most useful for deciding how to map generic R4 URLs, non-canonical R6 references, and the relationship semantics around `part-of`, `predecessor`, `successor`, and type-specific warnings.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Most R6 changes appear aimed at consolidating artifact representation and clarifying relationship semantics. Some disruption was avoidable: retaining `url` as deprecated or adding `url` as an `artifact[x]` choice would have preserved more R4 content directly.

## Follow-up analysis
Base datatype changes belong to the `DataType` and `Element` reports. Cross-version conversion maps and full spec change notes would materially improve confidence in migration recommendations.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 keeps the same `RelatedArtifact` identity but removes `url`, creating a direct R4-to-R6 validation break. The top migration concerns are mapping generic URLs, supporting the new `artifact[x]` and `resourceReference` representations, and handling the new required `part-of` code. The main uncertainty is the absence of an authoritative cross-version conversion map.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should first inventory R4 `RelatedArtifact.url` usage, because there is no mechanical same-name target in R6. Next, consumers and code generators need support for R6 choice properties such as `artifactMarkdown`, `artifactAttachment`, `artifactCanonical`, and `artifactReference`, while still reading deprecated legacy carriers. Finally, terminology handling must accept `part-of` in R6 but preserve or explicitly map it when producing R4.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for computable element, cardinality, type, constraint, and local CodeSystem changes because they are directly visible in the supplied package files. Confidence is lower for exact migration policy and semantic intent because official diffs, rendered change notes, Jira history, and cross-version ConceptMaps were not supplied.

findings.title: RelatedArtifact.url was removed in R6

semanticText.short: Where the artifact can be accessed
semanticText.definition: A url for the artifact that can be followed to access the actual content.
semanticText.comment: If a document or resource element is present, this element SHALL NOT be provided.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed a simple URL pointer to the related artifact as a first-class field.

newState.summary: `RelatedArtifact.url` is absent from the R6 snapshot and differential.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 has no same-name `url` element. The new `artifact[x]` choice supports `markdown`, `Attachment`, `canonical`, and `Reference`, but not primitive `url`.

facts.note: No R6 `artifact[x]` primitive url choice was found.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element id and path `RelatedArtifact.url` exist in R4 and have no corresponding R6 element. R6 adds other representation fields, but none is a direct same-name or same-type continuation.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation and serialization break for R4 instances that contain `url`: an R6 validator or strict parser should reject the unknown element. Generated R4 models with a `url` property cannot be reused against the R6 datatype without a transform or compatibility layer.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Losing a link to supporting documentation or evidence can affect auditability and knowledge-resource traceability, even when it is not a direct patient-safety data element.

justification.inferredGoal: Consolidate all artifact targets into reference, attachment, canonical, or markdown representations.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `RelatedArtifact.url` as a deprecated 0..1 `url` element, or add a primitive `url` choice to `artifact[x]`, while steering new content toward richer artifact forms.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of consolidating artifact targets into clearer typed representations is reasonable, but the hard removal of the R4 `url` carrier was probably avoidable. A generic access URL is not always equivalent to a FHIR canonical or an attachment URL, so preserving the old shape would have kept most R4-valid instances valid while still allowing R6 to prefer `artifact[x]` for more specific representations.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would keep `RelatedArtifact.url` in R6 as deprecated with clear precedence or exclusivity guidance, or include `url` as one of the `artifact[x]` choices. That would preserve existing R4 data and allow gradual migration. The tradeoff is an overlapping content model: producers might continue using the deprecated field indefinitely, and receivers would need rules for duplicate or inconsistent link representations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves most R4 URL instances with moderate duplicate-link representation and some ambiguity between generic URLs, attachment URLs, and canonicals.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `RelatedArtifact.url` as 0..1, type `url`, and summary.
R6 has no element with id or path `RelatedArtifact.url`.
R6 `artifact[x]` choices are `markdown`, `Attachment`, `canonical`, and `Reference`; primitive `url` is not included.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example is appropriate only when the R4 URL identifies document-like content that can be represented as an Attachment. A canonical FHIR artifact might instead map to `artifactCanonical`; a generic access URL may require manual policy or an extension.

findings.narrativeMd: `RelatedArtifact.url` is a local R4 element and is gone in R6. This affects any historical R4 knowledge artifact that used a plain URL rather than `document` or `resource`. The closest R6 alternatives are context-dependent, so the migration is not reliably syntactic.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid fragment containing `url` can become R6-invalid because the element is unknown in the R6 datatype. This is not merely a code-generation rename: R6 does not offer a primitive URL choice under `artifact[x]`, so strict round-trip transformation can lose the distinction between a generic access URL, an attachment URL, and a canonical FHIR artifact reference.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory all R4 `RelatedArtifact.url` occurrences. Map document downloads to `artifactAttachment.url`, canonical FHIR artifact URLs to `artifactCanonical` only when they are truly canonical references, and leave ambiguous generic URLs for manual review or an agreed extension. Add regression tests for documentation, citation, and resource-link cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The consolidation goal could have been met less disruptively by retaining `url` as deprecated or by adding `url` to `artifact[x]`. Removing it forces every producer to classify old URLs more specifically, which improves semantics but creates avoidable conversion risk.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 allowed `RelatedArtifact.url` as an optional primitive URL carrier, while R6 has no `RelatedArtifact.url` and `artifact[x]` does not include a primitive `url` choice. An R4 instance that used this field is therefore old-valid/new-invalid under the R6 datatype unless transformed. The break is path-local, but the migration is not purely mechanical because the same R4 URL might need to become an `Attachment.url`, a canonical artifact reference, a non-canonical reference, markdown citation text, or an extension depending on what the URL meant. That ambiguity makes the hard removal disproportionate enough to merit renewed review even though the R4 datatype was low maturity.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition snapshot has `RelatedArtifact.url` 0..1, type `url`, summary=true.
R6 StructureDefinition snapshot has no `RelatedArtifact.url` element.
R6 `RelatedArtifact.artifact[x]` choices are `markdown`, `Attachment`, `canonical`, and `Reference`, not primitive `url`.
R4 core package search found RelatedArtifact used across many knowledge-resource paths, but no quick evidence proving broad production use of this specific `url` path.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 RelatedArtifact is FMM 1/trial-use in the local maturity/status inputs, which lowers the stability expectation and prevents assuming broad production impact from the break alone. The judgment remains Revisit because this specific removal creates a direct old-valid/new-invalid failure and a potentially lossy, expert-dependent URL classification step.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 JSON containing `url` has an element that is absent from the R6 datatype, and there is no same-type primitive URL replacement.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking R6 base design plausibly exists: retain `url` as deprecated for one release, or include `url` as an `artifact[x]` choice with guidance preferring richer carriers. That would preserve most R4 instances while allowing R6 to steer new content. The tradeoff is duplicate/overlapping representations and receiver precedence rules, but that seems lower cost than forcing ambiguous URL reclassification at the base boundary.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing hard-break and less-breaking-alternative judgment, but the fresh assessment gives more weight to low FMM and therefore relies on the direct validation break plus lossy migration ambiguity rather than assuming broad production impact.

findings.title: R6 adds artifact[x] and Reference-based carriers that R4 cannot fully represent

oldState.summary: R4 used separate optional fields `citation`, `document`, `url`, and canonical `resource`; there was no `artifact[x]` or `resourceReference`.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 representation was spread across named fields, with only a canonical field for FHIR resources.

newState.summary: R6 retains the legacy fields but marks `citation`, `document`, and `resource` deprecated in favor of `artifact[x]`; it also adds `resourceReference`.

semanticText.definition: The related artifact represented as a canonical or direct reference to a FHIR resource, an Attachment, or directly inline as markdown.
semanticText.comment: For artifacts represented as FHIR resources, a canonical or Reference to the FHIR Resource.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 introduces choice-property serializations such as `artifactMarkdown`, `artifactAttachment`, `artifactCanonical`, and `artifactReference`, while `resourceReference` is also available but deprecated in favor of `artifact[x]`.

facts.newValue: citation/document/resource definitions begin with Deprecated in favor of the new artifact[x] element
`artifactReference` and `resourceReference` may carry non-canonical references not representable by R4 `resource`

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `artifact[x]` and `resourceReference` are new R6 element ids. Some `artifact[x]` choices correspond to R4 legacy carriers, but the R6 Reference choices do not have a full R4 equivalent.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4-to-R6 instances using `citation`, `document`, or `resource` can still validate, but R6 producers may emit new choice fields that R4 parsers reject. R6 `Reference` values also cannot be represented in R4's canonical-only `resource` field unless the target can be converted to a canonical URL.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Consumers that only inspect the legacy fields may miss citations, dependencies, or evidence references carried in `artifact[x]`.

justification.inferredGoal: Unify related artifact targets and support direct references to FHIR resources, attachments, and inline markdown.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: the new `artifact[x]` and `resourceReference` carriers are optional, and the R4 `citation`, `document`, and `resource` carriers remain structurally valid in R6.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Unifying artifact representations and adding direct `Reference` support are reasonable R6 goals, and the base design preserves R4 instances that use the retained legacy carriers. The high risk is mainly that R6 producers and generated R6 models may use new fields that R4 systems cannot parse or down-convert. Delaying deprecation text or publishing stronger dual-read guidance could reduce migration friction, but those are transition mitigations rather than a less-breaking base design needed to preserve R4-valid instances.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because this finding is primarily additive and R4-valid carrier fields remain present, no R4-to-R6 backward-compatible alternative applies. Keeping the legacy fields non-deprecated for longer or supplying normative mapping guidance could reduce operational confusion, but it would not change the core compatibility posture. Non-canonical `Reference` support also necessarily has no complete R4 equivalent because R4 only had the canonical `resource` carrier.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The added R6 expressivity creates R6-to-R4 conversion and consumer-update work, but it is not an R4-to-R6 base-design break.

evidence.detail: R4 has no `artifact[x]` or `resourceReference` element and uses canonical `resource` for related resources.
R6 definitions for `citation`, `document`, and `resource` state they are deprecated in favor of `artifact[x]`.

examples.examplesMd: The `artifactReference` example is validly shaped for the R6 choice element but has no direct R4 field unless the reference can be replaced by a canonical URL. The migration example shows a case that can down-map to R4 `resource`; not all references can.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 changes the representation model by adding `artifact[x]` and `resourceReference`. This is not a hard break for old R4 fragments that use retained fields, but it is a major runtime and conversion risk: generated R6 code will expose new choice properties and R4 systems will not know them.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R6 instances using `artifactMarkdown`, `artifactAttachment`, `artifactCanonical`, `artifactReference`, or `resourceReference` can be rejected by R4 validators as unknown elements. `artifactMarkdown`, `artifactAttachment`, and `artifactCanonical` often have plausible R4 targets (`citation`, `document`, and `resource`), but `artifactReference` and `resourceReference` are not cleanly representable when the target is a local or literal Reference rather than a canonical URL.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update serializers, parsers, search/indexing logic, and generated model bindings to read both legacy and `artifact[x]` fields. When producing R4, map `artifactMarkdown` to `citation`, `artifactAttachment` to `document`, and canonical artifacts to `resource` where safe. Treat non-canonical references as lossy and use extensions or manual review if R4 output is required.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The Reference support addresses a real expressivity gap in R4. However, deprecating legacy fields at the same time increases risk for consumers that only look at the old locations. A transition period with normative dual-write guidance would have been more backward compatible.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm whether the final R6 specification supplies official cross-version extensions for `artifactReference` or `resourceReference`; none was identified in the supplied local inputs.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds `artifact[x]` and `resourceReference` while retaining the R4 `citation`, `document`, and `resource` carriers, now marked deprecated in favor of `artifact[x]`. This is not a hard R4-to-R6 instance break for those retained fields. The real issue is runtime and down-conversion behavior: R6 producers can put related-artifact content in new choice properties that R4 parsers do not know, and `artifactReference` or `resourceReference` can carry non-canonical references that R4's canonical-only `resource` field cannot represent. That is real migration work, but the added expressivity and unified carrier model are reasonable, and the base design already preserves the old non-URL carriers.
keyEvidence: R6 snapshot adds `RelatedArtifact.artifact[x]` with `markdown`, `Attachment`, `canonical`, and `Reference` choices.
R4 snapshot has no `artifact[x]` or `resourceReference` and uses separate `citation`, `document`, `url`, and canonical `resource` carriers.
R6 definitions for `citation`, `document`, and `resource` say they are deprecated in favor of `artifact[x]` but the elements remain present.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Low R4 FMM softens the compatibility concern, especially because the change is mostly additive for R4-to-R6 validation. It does not erase the real R6-to-R4 and generated-client update burden, so the result is Breaking but probably OK rather than Revisit.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss and runtime/API/codegen: R6 `artifact[x]` choice names and `resourceReference` are unknown to R4 models, and Reference-valued artifacts are not always convertible to R4 canonical `resource`.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: There is no clearly better base R6 design that both preserves R4 and meets the goal. R6 already keeps the legacy `citation`, `document`, and `resource` fields, and avoiding `Reference` support would leave an expressivity gap. Stronger dual-read/dual-write guidance or slower deprecation could reduce operational friction, but those are transition mitigations more than less-breaking base structure alternatives.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing high runtime/conversion concern, but the fresh judgment treats the change as proportionate because it is additive for R4-to-R6 validation and retains the legacy non-URL fields.

findings.title: Required RelatedArtifact.type binding adds part-of and changes relationship definitions

oldState.summary: R4 `type` was required-bound to RelatedArtifactType 4.0.1 with eight codes.

binding.description: The type of relationship to the related artifact.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local R4 CodeSystem is complete and contains documentation, justification, citation, predecessor, successor, derived-from, depends-on, and composed-of.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 did not include a `part-of` relationship code.

newState.summary: R6 `type` remains required-bound but the value set version adds `part-of`; several definitions and the element comment are more specific.

binding.description: The type of relationship to the related artifact.

changedCodes.changeSummary: Definition now describes version ordering independent of status.
Definition now describes version ordering independent of status.
Definition now uses this artifact and target artifact wording and notes multiple targets.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: No R4 codes were removed. R6 adds `part-of` and refines several relationship definitions.

semanticText.short: documentation | justification | citation | predecessor | successor | derived-from | depends-on | composed-of | part-of
semanticText.comment: The R6 comment warns against using related artifact elements to create bi-directional resource links and gives directional guidance for FHIR resource relationships.

newState.narrativeMd: Because the binding is required, the added code is valid in R6 but invalid in R4 unless specially mapped.

facts.newValue: Short list includes part-of and comment adds directional link guidance

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same `RelatedArtifact.type` element and same canonical ValueSet are used in both versions, with a versioned required binding and a complete local CodeSystem in each package.

impact.impactRationaleMd: No R4 code was removed, so existing R4 `type` values remain valid in R6. The break is in the other direction: an R6 instance using `part-of` violates the R4 required binding and may fail generated enum parsing, validation, or switch logic.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Misinterpreting relationship direction can affect dependency graphs, evidence traceability, version ordering, and publication workflows.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent the inverse of `composed-of` and clarify relationship direction.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: adding `part-of` preserves all R4 `type` codes and creates only R6-to-R4 required-binding and enum risk.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Representing the inverse of `composed-of` and clarifying relationship direction are reasonable goals. Since no R4 code was removed, existing R4 instances remain valid in R6. The incompatibility is the closed R4 binding rejecting new R6 `part-of` values, which is an R6-to-R4 concern inherent in adding a core required-bound code.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No R4-to-R6-preserving alternative applies. Systems producing R4 can use an extension, a profile-specific convention, or reverse the relationship to `composed-of` when the target artifact is available, but those are conversion mitigations. The true base-design alternative would be not adding `part-of` as a core code, which would avoid the R4 enum problem but fail the R6 goal of a consistently understood inverse relationship.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 extensions, backports, or inverse `composed-of` mappings are down-conversion mitigations, not less-breaking R6 base designs; avoiding the core code would weaken interoperability.

evidence.detail: R6 binds `type` with strength `required` to `ValueSet/related-artifact-type|6.0.0-ballot4` and lists `part-of` in the short description.
The R6 complete CodeSystem adds `part-of`; the R4 complete CodeSystem does not contain it.
Definitions for `predecessor`, `successor`, `derived-from`, `depends-on`, and `composed-of` changed text between R4 and R6.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment is R6-valid with respect to the required `type` binding, but `part-of` is outside the R4 required value set. Mapping it to `composed-of` without changing the direction of the relationship would be semantically wrong.

findings.narrativeMd: `RelatedArtifact.type` keeps the same path, cardinality, and required binding strength, but the required code set expands. This is safe for R4-to-R6 validation but important for consumers that down-convert R6 or hard-code the R4 enum.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R6 fragment using `type: part-of` is not valid against the R4 required binding. R4 generated enum types may also reject the code before validation. Definition changes for existing codes are not hard validation breaks, but they can affect relationship-direction logic and graph traversal.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update R6 enum/code handling to include `part-of`. When producing R4, do not blindly map `part-of` to `composed-of`; either move the relationship to the opposite artifact if available, use an extension, or flag the record for manual review. Test unknown-code handling in parsers generated from R4 definitions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A new required code is the normal interoperable way to add a relationship. It is not backward compatible with R4's closed binding, but using only extensions would have made the R6 relationship less discoverable and less consistently supported.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The local CodeSystems are complete, so the added-code finding is strong. The practical mapping policy still needs human decision because relationship direction matters.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `RelatedArtifact.type` keeps the same path, cardinality, type, and required binding strength, but the R6 required value set adds `part-of` and refines several relationship definitions. No R4 code is removed, so existing R4 instances remain valid for this path when moving to R6. The compatibility issue is reverse-direction and enum-based: R6 content using `part-of` is outside the R4 required binding and may be rejected by R4 validators or generated R4 enum code. Adding an inverse relationship code is a normal and useful terminology evolution, and avoiding the code would weaken the R6 relationship model.
keyEvidence: R4 `RelatedArtifact.type` is 1..1 code with required binding to `ValueSet/related-artifact-type|4.0.1`.
R6 `RelatedArtifact.type` is still 1..1 code with required binding to `ValueSet/related-artifact-type|6.0.0-ballot4`.
R6 CodeSystem adds `part-of`; the R4 complete CodeSystem does not contain it.
R6 element comment adds directional guidance warning against bidirectional resource links.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Because the R4 content is FMM 1/trial-use, the reverse-direction enum incompatibility carries less standards-stability weight. The low maturity supports accepting a proportionate terminology expansion rather than revisiting it.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: `type = part-of` is valid in R6 but invalid against the R4 required binding and may fail R4 generated enum parsing; existing R4 codes remain valid in R6.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking R6 base alternative would be to avoid adding `part-of` or make it extension-only, but that would not meet the goal of a shared, required-bound inverse relationship code. Mapping to `composed-of` is not generally safe unless the relationship direction is reversed, so conversion guidance helps but is not a better base design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly identifies the R6-to-R4 required-binding and enum issue, but the fresh assessment downgrades the concern from a high-impact design problem because this is a widening R4-to-R6 change with a reasonable interoperability goal.

findings.title: R6 adds warning constraints tying type values to allowed representation carriers

oldState.summary: R4 root had only inherited `ele-1` as a computable constraint for this datatype.

semanticText.comment: Each related artifact is either an attachment, or a reference to another knowledge resource, but not both.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 described mutual exclusivity in prose but did not include type-specific warning constraints.

newState.summary: R6 adds local warning constraints `rla-1`, `rla-2`, and `rla-3`.

constraints.human: Citation must be inline or a canonical reference to a Citation
constraints.expression: type = 'citation' implies ((citation.exists() xor resource.exists()) or (artifact is markdown or artifact is canonical))
type = 'documentation' implies (document.exists() or artifact is Attachment)

constraints.human: Justification must be an attachment or a reference to an ArtifactAssessment
constraints.expression: type = 'justification' implies ((document.exists() or resourceReference.exists()) or (artifact is Attachment or artifact is Reference))

semanticText.comment: Each related artifact is either a reference to another knowledge resource, or represented directly inline as an Attachment or markdown.

newState.narrativeMd: The new constraints are warning-level, not error-level, but they materially affect validator output and conformance expectations.

facts.note: Warning constraints do not normally make an instance invalid, but some pipelines gate on warnings.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The constraints are present in the R6 `RelatedArtifact` root differential and snapshot with source `StructureDefinition/RelatedArtifact`; they are not inherited-only base constraints.

impact.impactRationaleMd: FHIR warning constraints do not normally invalidate an instance, so this is not a hard instance break. It can still break operational validation pipelines that treat warnings as release blockers, and it can expose semantically questionable R4 combinations that previously passed without this local warning.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The risk is primarily conformance and data-quality related; it could affect clinical knowledge traceability when citation, documentation, or justification links are represented with an unexpected carrier.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify which representation forms are appropriate for citations, documentation, and justifications.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the type-to-carrier guidance as narrative/base documentation instead of computable warning constraints.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of making citation, documentation, and justification carriers more consistent is reasonable. The added constraints can disrupt systems that treat warnings as fatal, but they do not make instances invalid under normal FHIR validation. A narrative-only approach would be less disruptive, yet it would not provide the same computable signal to validators, so the chosen warning-level design is probably justified despite a partial less-breaking path.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would leave the representation rules in the element definitions, comments, or implementation guidance without adding `rla-1`, `rla-2`, and `rla-3` as computable warning constraints. That would preserve R4-like validation output for existing data and avoid CI systems failing on warnings. The tradeoff is material: validators and data-quality dashboards would no longer consistently surface problematic carrier/type combinations, and implementers would have to discover the guidance manually.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids warning-gated pipeline disruption, but loses validator-discoverable and uniform guidance; warning severity is already a compatibility-preserving compromise.

evidence.detail: R4 root constraint list contains `ele-1` but no `rla-*` constraints.
R6 adds warning `rla-1` for citation representation.
evidence.quote: type = 'citation' implies ((citation.exists() xor resource.exists()) or (artifact is markdown or artifact is canonical))

evidence.detail: R6 adds warning `rla-2` for documentation representation.
evidence.quote: type = 'documentation' implies (document.exists() or artifact is Attachment)

evidence.detail: R6 adds warning `rla-3` for justification representation.
evidence.quote: type = 'justification' implies ((document.exists() or resourceReference.exists()) or (artifact is Attachment or artifact is Reference))

examples.examplesMd: The example is not R6-invalid solely because `rla-2` is warning severity, but it is R6-problematic: a validator should warn that documentation should be represented as an Attachment.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 makes previously prose-like expectations computable as warning constraints. This matters for validation dashboards, CI pipelines, and data-quality gates, especially for knowledge repositories that use `type` to decide how to render or retrieve related artifacts.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid fragments can become R6-warning-producing rather than R6-invalid. The compatibility impact depends on validator policy: systems that fail builds on warnings will experience this as breaking, while systems that distinguish warnings from errors will treat it as guidance.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review `type = citation`, `documentation`, and `justification` instances and align their carriers with the R6 warnings. Use `artifactMarkdown` or canonical citation references for citations, `artifactAttachment` or `document` for documentation, and Attachment or Reference forms for justifications. Add tests that assert expected warning behavior rather than treating all warnings as fatal.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because the new constraints are warnings, the specification chose a relatively backward-compatible mechanism. The remaining disruption comes from local operational policy, not from base FHIR validity.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The human text for `rla-3` mentions ArtifactAssessment, but the computable expression only tests for Reference/Attachment shapes. A reviewer should confirm intended target typing in final R6 materials.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds three local warning constraints linking selected `type` values to expected representation carriers: citation should be inline or canonical citation-related content, documentation should be an attachment, and justification should be an attachment or reference. These warnings can change validator output and can disrupt CI or publication processes that fail on warnings, but they do not make an instance structurally invalid under ordinary FHIR validation. The constraints also appear aimed at improving consistent rendering and data quality for the newly unified carrier model. Given warning severity and low R4 maturity, this is a proportionate compatibility pressure rather than a change that needs renewed base-design review.
keyEvidence: R4 root `RelatedArtifact` constraint list contains inherited `ele-1` but no `rla-*` local constraints.
R6 adds warning `rla-1`: citation must be inline or a canonical reference to a Citation.
R6 adds warning `rla-2`: documentation must be an attachment.
R6 adds warning `rla-3`: justification must be an attachment or a reference to an ArtifactAssessment.
All three new `rla-*` constraints have severity `warning`, not `error`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 1/trial-use substantially softens the stability concern. Because the new constraints are warning-level, low FMM makes it inappropriate to infer major production breakage from changed validation output alone.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: warning-level: R4-valid combinations can produce new R6 warnings, and warning-as-error pipelines may fail, but base R6 validity is not lost solely because these constraints warn.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design would leave the carrier/type guidance as prose or implementation guidance only. That would preserve R4-like warning output, but it would also remove a computable, uniform data-quality signal. Warning severity is already a compromise compared with error constraints, so the less-breaking alternative has a material interoperability tradeoff.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing warning-level operational concern, but the fresh review treats the impact as proportionate and not a high base-spec break because the constraints are warnings and low-FMM content has weaker stability expectations.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The R6 StructureDefinition is present at the expected path and keeps the same canonical URL, id, name, kind, abstract flag, and type. The base-definition shift is inherited/global and excluded from findings.

For elements that exist in both versions (`type`, `label`, `display`, `citation`, `document`, and `resource`), min/max cardinalities are unchanged. New R6 elements are optional; the removed `url` element is reported separately.

Shared local elements retain their R4 types: `type` is `code`, `label`/`display` are `string`, `citation` is `markdown`, `document` is `Attachment`, and `resource` is canonical to `Resource`. New type-domain choices are covered by findings.
No local `RelatedArtifact` element changed `isModifier`; all checked local elements remain non-modifier.
The shared local elements that were summary elements in R4 remain summary elements in R6; new R6 local representation elements are also summary elements.
No local slicing was found on the `RelatedArtifact` content model. The inherited open slicing on `extension` is out of scope.
No local fixed value, pattern value, or default value constraints were found in either version.
No local maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue restrictions were found on `RelatedArtifact` elements.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Maturity/status metadata changed from draft trial-use to active normative
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The canonical identity and instance content model identity remain the same; maturity metadata does not by itself invalidate instances.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance, dependency policy, and generated documentation may treat the R6 datatype as more stable or normative than the R4 draft/trial-use artifact.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Legacy citation, document, and resource carriers are retained but deprecated in text
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The R6 elements keep the same paths, cardinalities, and types, so existing instances using those fields remain structurally valid.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: New R6 producers should prefer `artifact[x]`; consumers should read both old and new carriers during transition.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Root description expands scope to dependencies and components
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The description broadens explanatory text but does not add required elements or remove old relationship types.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Documentation and UI labels may need updates because R6 positions `RelatedArtifact` as covering dependencies and components in addition to documentation, justification, and citations.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 changes `RelatedArtifact.baseDefinition` from `Element` to `DataType`. Per scope instructions, this global datatype hierarchy shift is excluded from local findings and should be assessed in the base datatype report.
Inherited `id` and `extension` behavior, including extension constraints and base `ele-1`, should be handled by the `Element`/base artifact analyses rather than duplicated here.
A normative conversion map would resolve how to handle removed `url`, new `artifact[x]` choices, non-canonical references, and `part-of` down-conversion.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The analysis did not include an official R4-to-R6 diff page or ballot change notes, so rationale and intended migration sequencing are inferred from computable definitions.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the official rendered diff, change proposal, or Jira history for `RelatedArtifact`.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No authoritative cross-version ConceptMap or StructureMap was supplied. Mapping recommendations for `url`, `artifactReference`, `resourceReference`, and `part-of` are therefore engineering guidance rather than normative conversion rules.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Use an official R4/R6 conversion map or published cross-version extension guidance.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology comparison used the local complete CodeSystem resources rather than a terminology-server expansion. This is sufficient to identify the added `part-of` code, but a server expansion would independently confirm package/version behavior.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run expansions for `ValueSet/related-artifact-type` in both versions with a terminology server.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 input is ballot build `6.0.0-ballot4`, not a final normative release. Findings are accurate for the supplied package but may change before final publication.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Re-run the assessment against the final R6 core package when available.
